summary: Warsh's Jackson Hole speech reset the September rate decision, with odds of a hold falling sharply after he doubled down on inflation concerns — hike probability had been near 70% before his remarks. Meanwhile, U.S. 50% tariffs on Canadian goods took effect August 22, and Canada countered with retaliatory tariffs ranging from 15% to 50% across a broad range of goods.
tweet: September rate hike odds surged 17 points post-Warsh while U.S.-Canada trade talks collapsed, triggering 50% tariffs on $20B of Canadian goods — two live risks keeping stocks rangebound and bonds bid.
